submitter: bugs_open/204 lane (stored slot identity at the remaining call sites)
rationale:
bugs_open/204's originally-filed defect (plan_sections, the build path) was fixed and proven live at v1.0.1259. What is still open is the same blindness at a THIRD call site, contributed to the file on 2026-08-20: ValidateSitePlanAction's validate_components arm. It DELETES an unresolvable section name where plan_sections merely defers one.

A decomposed page's sections are POSITIONAL slot names (prose-0, tool-1). They are not a content_components.name or .function under any spelling — the component each one is lives on page_components.component_id. componentNameResolver's key space is the catalogue, so it can never resolve them, and each of its four call sites drops what it cannot resolve.

MEASURED 2026-08-21, and this is the figure the change rests on: of the 140 PLAN_SECTION_NAME_DROPPED rows recorded fleet-wide since bugs_open/282's durable record shipped on 08-16, ONE HUNDRED AND FORTY are positional slot names (prose-0 x70, tool-1 x34, prose-2 x18, tool-0 x12, prose-1 x6) across 41 distinct pages, all from action='validate_plan'. Zero are display-name variants, typos or stale functions. The class this resolver exists to catch has produced no records at all; the class it cannot see has produced every one. That result could easily have come out as a mixture, which is what makes it evidence rather than illustration. It is also a LOWER BOUND, not a total — the record only exists from 08-16.

The damage is not theoretical. On 2026-08-20 a replan canary at loanandmortgagecalculator.co.uk emptied pages.sections on 41 of 45 live pages and filed 20 needs_page + 12 sibling items that would have built empty pages over live ones. Detected pre-fire, contained, reversed from a snapshot within the hour. pages.sections is the ONLY record of a decomposed page's composition: page_components keeps serving, so nothing looks wrong, and the next rebuild has nothing to rebuild.

Population at risk today [MEASURED 2026-08-21]: 107 section names across 7 sites resolve to no component by name or function (was 86 across 5 at filing on 08-05). validate_components is live on two agents, build-site-planner and site-planner.

THE CONSTRAINT THIS DESIGN IS BUILT AROUND. LANDMINES.md's entry on this exact footprint (added 2026-08-16 by the 282 lane) forbids the obvious fix: 'do NOT fix the inconsistency by widening loadComponentNameResolver itself. Three of its four call sites are apply_gap_plan_action.go, whose menu 407 and register PLAN-049 record as deliberately not widened. A resolver-level widening hands that path an authority an owner-facing decision withheld, silently and with no config to show for it.' So the resolver is untouched. Instead each drop branch consults, per page, whether the page already carries a slot under that name. A menu widening enlarges what may be newly PLACED anywhere; this grants no placement at all — only 'keep what this page already has'. The distinction is a property of the map key, not a claim in a comment, and TestStoredSlotRescue_IsScopedToTheProposedPage is what makes it so: a slot stored on another page of the same site rescues nothing.

RFC SCOPE, ruled rather than dodged. The sentence that changes is validate_components' own comment: 'every surviving section name is a valid component function'. Per owner ruling 2026-07-29 §1 a guarantee change is the RFC trigger, so it needs arguing. Three grounds for normal council scope: (a) RFC_002's worked trigger ran the OTHER way — an evaluator GAINING a destructive power (refute where it had only confirmed); this REMOVES a destructive power and grants none downstream. (b) Downstream already meets these names by the estate's own decided design — pages.sections carries positional names on 7 live sites today and the readers were built for them (bugs_closed/182, 13252f714, PBP-035's stored_slot_name, revalidateNeedsPage's slot_name match). Validate was enforcing a stale invariant against stores the platform had already moved past; preserving restores the status quo ante rather than minting a new shape. (c) The new guarantee is narrower than it sounds and is checkable: 'a valid component function, OR the slot name of a stored row on that same page' — page-local and realised. The guarantee sentence is rewritten in the same commit and the register entry (PLAN-027) amended in the same commit, per the ordering exemption's condition 2.

NO CONFIG KEY, deliberately, and this is the decision most likely to draw an objection. The 2026-08-02 §2 rule targets a seam whose widest branch is licensed by 'callers must all be X' — a caller property enforced by comment. This arm's licence is page-local stored data enforced by a map key. Further: the two sibling call sites of this same judgement (plan_sections Path 0, 182's rerender) both run unconditionally and both were council-approved; making the third opt-in would recreate the half-fixed asymmetry that IS bug 204. And the unsafe default would be OFF-ness itself — default-OFF preserves the behaviour that emptied 41 pages, on every site, until config names each agent. No optional key is added, so the WFA-013 budget is untouched; which also matters because validate_site_plan has NO RegisterActionInputSpec at all (207 exist across the estate), so any key added to it would be invisible to the optional-key audit. That missing spec is noted as a separate task, not smuggled in here.

SOURCE OF TRUTH — a correction to the bug file's own 08-20 contribution, which proposed trusting the page's realised pages.sections. That names the wrong store twice: it is the column the bug destroys (so after one un-fixed run the 'source of truth' says the page has nothing), and it reaches validate through the existing_pages field, which site-planner does not have — its live step list is [complete, load_available_components, load_style_collections, plan_site, validate_plan], with no load_existing_pages step, so a fix keyed on that field is structurally inert on one of the two live consumers. page_components is the ground truth and is what plan_sections already chose.

SCOPE OF THE FIX: three of the four drop branches. applyNewPage is deliberately excluded — a genuinely new page has no page_components rows, so a positional name proposed for it points at nothing and dropping it is correct; a test pins that so nobody 'fixes' it later. The two gap-plan arms are LATENT exposure, not measured damage: content-gap-planner is live (46 gap_plan_* items, most recent 08-20) but has recorded zero drops since 08-16. Stated as latent deliberately — the evidence there is the code path, not a row.

The write-side guard on upsertPage's unconditional `sections = EXCLUDED.sections` (whose nav_label and meta_description siblings in the SAME statement were given destructive-write guards on 08-19) is a separate commit and a separate submission: different mechanism, different blast radius (three live agents), and a class defence rather than this bug's fix.

plan.summary: Two commits, one coherent task. A: extract plan_sections' proven slot-identity loader into datahelpers as ONE shared reader (pure move — per-page projection byte-identical, its seven existing sqlmock tests pass unmodified), with membership as a SEPARATE pure derivation that deliberately does not inherit the id map's conflict rule. B: consult it, per page, at three of the four drop branches, only after the resolver and its menu union have both missed; keep the entry VERBATIM (facts intact, name not collapsed onto its component function); fail toward keeping on a read error; and file one durable summary row per run so 'the arm fired' is distinguishable from 'nothing needed rescuing'. componentNameResolver is untouched. 17 tests, 7 mutations run and all 7 killed.

edits.symbol: PageSlotRow / PageSlotIdentitiesSQL / PageSlotIdentitiesForSiteSQL / LoadPageSlotRows / LoadPageSlotRowsForSite / SlotIDMap / SlotNameSet
edits.rationale: New file on the LOCK-008 pattern, not a hunk in a hot shared file. The same blindness had been fixed THREE times in three private loaders (182 re-render, 13252f714 build, and now validation) — a fourth copy is how the third came to exist. One shared predicate, two projections over it, two PURE derivations. The separation of SlotIDMap from SlotNameSet is the load-bearing decision: the id question must refuse a slot whose repeats disagree (an ambiguous carry source is no carry source), the MEMBERSHIP question must not inherit that rule, because for membership a legitimate repeat still means the page HAS the slot and answering no would delete a live section. Predicate deliberately narrow — no build_status <> 'removed' filter, because adding one would change plan_sections' behaviour under cover of a refactor; a test refuses a build_status clause so it cannot drift in.

Unify NOW rather than later: two hand-maintained copies of one judgement is the drift class this council reviews for, and 'unify later' is how a seam becomes folklore. Contained by phasing — this is behaviour-identical, its seven sqlmock tests pass UNMODIFIED (the disconfirming check for 'the extraction changed behaviour'), and it lands before anything behavioural. The log/error strings are preserved because 204's own closure evidence pod-greps them; SlotIDMap takes a caller prefix for exactly that reason.

The judgement, in its own file so the hot shared v3_site_actions.go takes only a small hunk (a same-file passenger from a concurrent session cannot be prevented by any pathspec). Three-valued on purpose: a boolean would collapse 'this page does not carry that slot' (drop is right) into 'I could not find out' (drop is the incident). Lazy — the site's rows are read at most once and only on the FIRST miss, so a site whose names are honest functions issues no extra query and the arm is inert on the undecomposed estate by construction rather than by configuration. Fails toward KEEPING, because the costs are asymmetric: a junk name surviving is deferred loudly one step later by plan_sections, an emptied decomposed page is recoverable only from a snapshot somebody thought to take.

The primary site — the only one with measured damage. Consulted strictly INSIDE the existing `if !ok` branch, so it runs only after all five resolver arms and the menu union have missed and can never rebind or shadow a name the catalogue resolves. The entry is kept VERBATIM: rewriting a positional name to its component's function would collapse prose-0 and prose-1 onto one name, which is precisely what the positional naming exists to prevent (the bug file's own candidate-3 rejection), and it would break the page's next id-first resolution. The keep is durably recorded ONCE per run, not per keep — a decomposed site rescues 40-70 names in one replan and 70 rows would bury the drops that still matter; but without any record 'the fix works' and 'the planner proposed only catalogue names this time' produce identical evidence, which is the resolvedViaMenu lesson from 282's own round.

Two of the three gap-plan drop branches. applyRetypeExisting matters most of the three because it writes `sections = $3::jsonb` straight onto a LIVE page, so a dropped positional name there is not a lost plan entry but a destroyed record. applyNewPage is deliberately LEFT: a genuinely new page has no page_components rows, so a positional name proposed for it points at nothing and dropping it is correct — and a test pins that, so the omission reads as a decision rather than an oversight. Exposure here is LATENT, not measured: content-gap-planner is live (46 gap_plan_* items, most recent 08-20) but has recorded zero PLAN_SECTION_NAME_DROPPED rows since 08-16, so the evidence is the code path.

Pins the extraction and the divergence. PerPageProjectionIsTheOnePlanSectionsShipped fails if the moved SQL stops being byte-identical to what 13252f714 shipped — the disconfirming check for 'this was a pure move'. BothProjectionsShareOnePredicate fails if someone edits one WHERE clause and leaves the other, which would make 'which component is at this slot' and 'does this page carry this slot' answer about different row sets. SlotNameSet_DoesNotInheritTheIDMapsConflictRule is the divergence pinned rather than asserted. WarningNamesItsCaller pins the pod-greppable substring 204's own closure evidence depends on. Mutations run and killed: conflict deletion removed (2 tests fail), SlotNameSet made to inherit the rule (divergence test fails), warning string altered (its test fails).

edits.symbol: 9 tests over the rescue arm, end to end through ValidateSitePlanAction
edits.rationale: Each assertion has a named disconfirming result. IsScopedToTheProposedPage is the load-bearing one: a slot stored on ANOTHER page of the same site must rescue nothing, which is what makes the not-a-widening argument a property of the code rather than a claim in a comment. IssuesNoQueryWhenEveryNameResolves uses sqlmock's ExpectationsWereMet to turn 'we think it is lazy' into an assertion, so 'inert on the undecomposed estate' is checked rather than reasoned. UnstoredUnresolvableNameIsStillDropped is the regression guard for the checker's real job. KeptObjectEntryRetainsItsFacts covers the RFC_016 facts that died with the entry pre-fix, because the drop precedes the object->string split. ReadFailureKeepsRatherThanDrops pins failing-toward-keeping. Mutations run and killed: keep removed; scope widened from page to site; slotUnknown made to drop; kept name rewritten to its component function.

Ordering-exemption condition 2: a shared seam is registered in the SAME commit that ships it, with its landmine and its open question, because later is how a seam becomes folklore. PLAN-051 registers the shared reader and states why a per-page rescue is not the resolver widening PLAN-050's own landmine forbids. PLAN-027's amendment states the CHANGED GUARANTEE explicitly ('a valid component function, OR the slot name of a stored row on that same page') rather than leaving it in a code comment, and records the 140-of-140 measurement. The one-line index row in 000_concept_index.md rides the same commit (the index is a generated-style table whose count is maintained by the concept-register-drift-check, DOC-074, so only the row is added by hand).
